features.name: number_led_sentence_count
features.definition: How many sentences across the counter-argument comments begin with a number?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of strings; malformed or missing -> null; empty list -> 0. For each comment, split into sentences with a regex splitting on (?<=[.!?])\s+ and on newlines/blank lines (also treat list-item lines as separate sentences). Strip leading whitespace and leading markdown/bullet characters (*, -, >, #, opening quotes/parentheses/brackets). A sentence is number-led if it then matches ^\d+([.,]\d+)*(%|st|nd|rd|th|s)?\b, i.e. starts with a digit character. Spelled-out numbers (e.g. 'Two') are not counted. Output the total count of number-led sentences summed across all comments. Raw mechanical count with no semantic filtering; ordinal list markers like '1.' or '1)' at the sentence start are counted as number-led.

h0: number_led_sentence_count has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
h1: Higher number_led_sentence_count is associated with a higher probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP changed view). "More sentences" is operationalized as the raw count across all supplied counter-comments, not a share; the count is not length-adjusted, and the supplied comments may be a subset. Numbered-list markers (e.g. '1.') count as number-led, and spelled-out numbers are excluded. Raw text may contain outcome announcements, and comment timing is unknown. This describes an association, not a causal effect.
